newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise despite dumping, mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise despite dumping, mood cautious.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose slightly despite a certain amount of dumping after disappointing April trade and current account figures on Wednesday, with dealers seeing a wary mood prevailing for the rest of the day.
"We have seen some selling out of long bonds, mainly the upcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark, the mood will be cautious up to Friday's U.S. June PPI data," one dealer said.

The tone-setting eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.15 point from the start at 113.91, yielding 5.89 percent while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark put on 0.12 point to 106.68, with the yield at 6.10 percent.

Turnover in the two key bonds was 2.3 billion and 4.2 billion crowns respectively. The 2006's September future rose 0.34 point to 113.32 with 28 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 edged 0.02 point up to 92.15.
The crown traded at a static 3.8080 per mark at 1115 gmt, unchanged from the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 58.
